stem: Which childhood cancer usually requires about 2 years of treatment rather than a 6-12 month multi-agent chemotherapy protocol?
explanation: ALL is the exception because it usually requires about 2 years of treatment, whereas most other childhood cancers are treated with multi-agent protocols over 6-12 months.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because ALL is the notable exception that usually needs around 2 years of treatment.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because AML is not the usual 2-year exception to the standard 6-12 month pattern.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because Ewing sarcoma is not the diagnosis classically associated with a 2-year chemotherapy duration.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because osteosarcoma is not the exception described for prolonged treatment duration.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because rhabdomyosarcoma is not the usual diagnosis requiring about 2 years of treatment.
